![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/597125714057269b7adf9c0a2a9bbdde9631cf37bc80518281ab4444c3189717.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>a)=P(Z<-a)=Φ(-a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z<-2.21).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/bafe03ed398bfbf95124eb389918759ca80c17eb37f32c2eacf98b48df4b05bc.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z>2.21).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/57eec4175c2f6d8b11db24548f973f9ab4a5b980a9e204352655b40cfd4e431f.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<-2.21) & =P(Z>2.21) \\  & =1-P(Z<2.21) \\  & =1-Φ(2.21) \\  & =1-0.9864 \\  & =0.0136.\end{aligned}
$$
